bib.title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development

question: Can role-specialised LLM agents, guided by a chat chain and communicative dehallucination, cooperate through language to produce complete, executable software across design, coding and testing?
hypothesis: Structuring multi-agent dialogue along a waterfall chat chain, with agents asking for specifics before answering, reduces coding hallucinations and yields better software than single-agent or fixed-SOP baselines.
contributions: ChatDev: a chat-powered software development framework with chat chain and communicative dehallucination
SRDD, a dataset of 1,200 software requirement descriptions
Analysis showing natural language helps system design and programming-language communication helps debugging

method.summary: Agents with roles (CEO, CTO, programmer, reviewer, tester) work in pairs (instructor and assistant) along a chain of 5 subtasks in 3 phases (design, coding, testing). Only each subtask's solution is passed forward as long-term memory. Communicative dehallucination lets the assistant ask the instructor for specifics before answering.
method.task: autonomous software development from a short natural-language requirement

datasets.name: SRDD (Software Requirement Description Dataset)
datasets.split: 5 categories (Education, Work, Life, Game, Creation), 40 subcategories, 30 prompts each
datasets.source: built by the authors from existing software descriptions on Ubuntu, Google Play, Microsoft Store, Apple Store; LLM generation plus human-guided post-processing

other.note: the LLM behind all agents and baselines; exact snapshot not stated

inference.samples: not stated (one run per task implied; no seeds)
inference.prompting: inception prompting: instructor and assistant system prompts cover subtask overview, roles, tools, protocol, termination, constraints

parameters.subtask termination: after two unchanged code modifications or 10 rounds of communication
parameters.phases: 3 phases, 5 subtasks (design; code writing and completion; code review and system testing)

metrics.name: Completeness
metrics.definition: percentage of software without any placeholder code snippets

metrics.name: Executability
metrics.definition: percentage of software that compiles and runs directly

metrics.name: Consistency
metrics.definition: cosine distance between embeddings of requirements and generated code (comments excluded), higher is more consistent

metrics.name: Quality
metrics.definition: product of completeness, executability and consistency

metrics.name: Pairwise win rate
metrics.definition: GPT-4 and human experts pick the preferred of two solutions

eval.protocol: Metrics averaged over all tasks; p<=0.05 marks significant difference from ChatDev; pairwise by GPT-4 and humans with order randomised. Number of human raters, embedding model, and test count not stated.

availability.data: SRDD in the same repository (per abstract: code and data available)

results.quote: ChatDev significantly raises the Quality from 0.1523 to 0.3953.

limits: Authors concede agents implement simple logic with low information density; suited to prototypes, not complex real-world apps
Evaluation lacks functionality, robustness, safety, user-friendliness; no function-level test cases or pass@k
Multi-agent costs more tokens and time than single agent
Quality is a product of three proxies; consistency is an embedding cosine, differing only slightly between methods
Only ChatGPT-3.5; seeds, number of runs, human raters, embedding model and exact model snapshot not stated; SRDD built by the authors
Baselines run on ChatDev's own dataset and metrics

terms.definition: the assistant takes an instructor-like role and requests more specific information before delivering a formal response
sequential phases each comprising sequential subtasks, each a multi-turn dialogue between an instructor and an assistant

lineage.note: inception prompting and pairwise human/GPT-4 evaluation setting
